purpose: One name per question a public input answers. The Framework grew three different meanings under the word type, and a developer could not tell from the name which one a component meant. The axes below fix the question each name answers; the alias map records every legacy name that still works, so a rename never breaks a consumer.

axes.appearance: How the control looks: default, tonal, outline, ghost, link, surface, filled, bordered, segmented.
axes.status: What the control reports about the world: success, warning, error, info, neutral.
axes.kind: What the control carries or is: an icon, an avatar, a checkbox, a folder, a file.

control_status.$comment: Decision C13 (docs review R031, 2026-11-08): a dangerous action and an error are different words. A control -- a button, an icon button, a menu item -- says danger: it deletes, discards or cannot be undone. A message -- a field, an alert, a badge, a toast, the alert bar -- says error: something went wrong. One red: danger is drawn with the error roles. On a control, error is danger's dated alias, the reverse of status_aliases, which a message keeps.

entries.menu-context: an entry's status (danger; error read as danger) or danger: true

rules: A new public input that answers one of these questions uses the axis name, never type.
A legacy name keeps working through the prop's aliases, and is listed here until it is retired.
The canonical name wins when both are set on the same element.
A component may carry several axes at once, because they answer different questions: a tag can be a checkbox (kind) reporting success (status) drawn as a ghost (appearance).

components.note: a destructive control is a status, not a colour role: `scheme` keeps saying which colour family a button takes and `status` says what it is about. A control's status is danger (control_status, decision C13); error and critical are its dated aliases. Only danger is painted, with the error roles.
the same split as buttons: the colour family stays `scheme`, what the control is about is `status` (control_status: danger, error its dated alias), and only danger is painted.
the class verification's two looks by sf-input's names: bordered cells, or filled cells (sf-verification--filled).
the class accordion's appearances by name: default is the filled surface, outline and flush its two modifiers.
the class menu's presentations by name: default, documentation-tree and compact, its two modifiers.

segmented draws the radiogroup as a sunken track with a plate under the selected segment (simai/ui-source#4); since 1.4.0 (owner decision D11b, 2026-11-08) the track is the default, `buttons` keeps the joined outlined buttons for forms, and the old values segmented and default answer as track and buttons until 2027-01-01.
`primary` was a colour role inside a list of statuses; since owner decision C131 (1) it is answered as the empty default, which draws primary, while neutral is grey
the skeleton's `type` is not part of this axis: it marks a placeholder standing in for an icon, which combines with any shape, so merging it into kind would make two combinable answers exclusive
the split: `type` answered both questions from one list, and still does — a status word given as type reaches the status axis, a content word reaches the kind axis

the split: `scheme` mixed colour roles with status words. `scheme` is not retired — it keeps answering which semantic colour the badge takes — but a status word given there is routed to the status axis, and the CSS matches the canonical class beside the legacy danger
primary was a colour inside a list of statuses; here it meant info

sf-chart-metric lives in the chart set (simai/ui-chart). Its status is the page's statement about the number in the shared vocabulary, a dot of that tone and the hint; the tile never infers it from the value (ui-chart M1, need 9). A package component is recorded here because the package runs tests/public-api-axes.contract.test.mjs in its overlay of ui-source, against this file, and a package file may not replace a ui-source one.

not_an_axis.scheme: which colour family a control uses (primary, secondary, on-surface). It is not an appearance -- the same appearance exists in every scheme -- and it is not a status: what a control is about is the status axis.
not_an_axis.mode: how a control behaves rather than how it looks (a modal loading inline or over ajax, a dropdown selecting or tagging).
not_an_axis.native-type: the HTML type attribute of a native element, which belongs to the platform, not to us.

data_state.rule: A component that shows data it is given or fetches (a table, a chart, a list) says where that data stands in one input, data-state, with the data states of standard simai.dynamic-composite-component (data-states-declared: at least loading, populated, empty and error; auto lets the component decide from the data). It is not the status axis: error here means the data could not be had, not a statement about the world. A data-state whose values are all data states needs no exemption of its own, in the Framework or in a package; one that offers any other word is held to the axes like every other input.
data_state.note: ready is the word the chart set (simai/ui-chart) uses for populated; it is recognised so the set's charts are not each exempted by hand (ui-chart M0, part 2), and a new component writes populated.

exempt_properties.reason: the value names the colour family the data's steps are drawn in -- a sequential or diverging scale over the Framework's role families, so a word like warning names a hue family of the data, not a status the control reports about the world.
exempt_properties.kept_for: sf-chart-heatmap lives in the chart package (simai/ui-chart). The package runs tests/public-api-axes.contract.test.mjs in its overlay of ui-source, against this file, and a package file may not replace a ui-source one (ui-chart msg-4445239656ac4dc3b461, 2026-11-03).

exempt_properties.reason: the value names the colour family the map's sequential steps are drawn in, so a word like success or warning names a hue family of the data, not a status the control reports about the world.
exempt_properties.kept_for: sf-chart-map lives in the chart package (simai/ui-chart f5a5a35). The package runs tests/public-api-axes.contract.test.mjs in its overlay of ui-source, against this file, and a package file may not replace a ui-source one (ui-chart msg-70d7f2970755492e8bd1, 2026-11-05).

exempt_properties.reason: a lifecycle state of the data — auto, loading, populated, empty, error — not a status the control reports about the world. The word error appears in both, which is why the exemption is written down rather than inferred.
exempt_properties.kept_for: sf-view-table lives in the SIMAI Framework Pro package (package pro, the component folder in simai/ui-pro; package larena from 2026-10-11 to 2026-11-02), and no free component declares data-state. It is keyed by the package folder, view-table since rename plan R2 (table before 2026-11-03). The exemption stays here because the package runs tests/public-api-axes.contract.test.mjs in its overlay of ui-source, against this file, and a package file may not replace a ui-source one.

exempt_properties.reason: the value names which icon set the glyph comes from — outlined, rounded, sharp — and the same word keys the loader's global default in SF_BOOT_CONFIG.icons.type, SF.Loader.getDefaultIconType and SF_ICON_TYPE. Renaming only the attribute would split one concept across two names, so this one is left alone deliberately.
a legacy name for file-size: the file's own size as text (12 KB), not a step of the size ladder. It is honoured and documented as legacy; a renderer passes file-size and never size.

the value names what the step does in the wizard -- info shows a text, form takes answers, action runs work, review shows the plan, result says what came of it -- so info is the kind of step, not a status the step reports; its outcome is the state value (done, skipped, running, error).

the value is where the step stands in the wizard's process -- not started, done, skipped, running, or error after its action failed -- the same stages sf-steps draws (completed, skipped, running, error), not a status of the world the step reports; the step's message says what happened.

backdrop (surface or color) tells the control what it stands on, so it takes the ink of that place (owner decisions C14, D11c, 2026-11-08). The value surface names the kind of place under the control -- a surface, a coloured place, a photo -- not a look of the control, so it answers where the control stands, not the appearance question.
exempt_properties.kept_for: the appearance of the control stays its own setting; backdrop only changes the ink the look is drawn in.

exempt_properties.reason: backdrop (surface, color or media) tells the control what it stands on, so it takes the ink of that place (owner decisions C14, D11c, 2026-11-08). The value surface names the kind of place under the control -- a surface, a coloured place, a photo -- not a look of the control, so it answers where the control stands, not the appearance question.
exempt_properties.kept_for: the appearance of the control stays its own setting; backdrop only changes the ink the look is drawn in.

exempt_properties.reason: the value says where the file's upload stands -- ready when it is there, uploading, or error when it did not upload (decision C81, the upload core's rows) -- the lifecycle of one file, as sf-file-download's state is; error names that outcome, not a status the control reports about the world, and the control has no status axis.

the value says where the file's preparation stands -- ready, preparing, or error when the application could not make the file (decision C25) -- the lifecycle of one request, as sf-confirm's state is; error names that outcome, not a status the control reports about the world, and the control has no status axis.

size_ladder.note: A component uses the steps it needs, but it uses these names. `full` is not a step: it means as wide as the viewport.

name_aliases.note: `input-size` named the inner field's size; `size` is the name every field uses. Both reach the same field.

change_event.rule: Every form value control reports a committed change as `change` on its host, once per change made by the user. A value set from code is not a change. A native control's `change` bubbles from its inner input; a composite control dispatches a `change` CustomEvent on its host. Older names stay emitted with the same detail as aliases for as long as the change journal (contracts/changes/journal.json) keeps them in compatibility; the manifest marks `change` with `canonical: true` and each alias with `alias_of: "change"`.

aliases.note: Also emitted by select() and clear().
`sf-datepicker-change` was named the preferred event; `change` now is.
The legacy names also fire when a value is set from code; `change` does not.
